project_description.value: Mechanical engineering services for existing climate control infrastructure survey and design of new copper pipe distribution system serving conservation climate-controlled display cases throughout the first floor of the Donald W. Reynolds Museum and Education Center at George Washington's Mount Vernon. Scope includes: existing conditions survey of active climate control piping serving display cases; new 2" copper pipe distribution mains; new 3/4" copper pipe branch lines; manual ball valves at each display case technical compartment; 2x2x2" copper tees; 12x12 wall-mounted access panels; and flexible silicon tube connections to individual display cases. Existing 3" copper pipe from lower-level conservation machine serves as the supply source.

sheets.title: FIRST FLOOR HVAC PLAN
sheets.source_file: 2025.04.22 MVLA EXISTING CLIMATE CONTROL INFRASTRUCTURE FINAL.pdf
sheets.reading_notes: First floor HVAC plan at 3/32" = 1'-0" scale showing the museum's first floor gallery layout with named exhibit areas (Be Washington, Revolutionary War, Making the American Army, Coalition Builder, Mount Vernon, etc.). New 2" copper pipe mains are shown routed from the upper left (where existing 3" copper pipe from lower level conservation machine terminates) through the gallery corridors to reach display cases throughout the floor. New 3/4" copper pipe serves branching connections at some areas. Manual ball valves (MBV) are located at the technical compartment under each display case (typ.). 2x2x2" copper tees at branch takeoffs. 12x12 wall-mounted access panels. Flexible silicon tube connections from copper pipe down inside wall to flex connection for display case (typical). Construction Notes: (1) per 2018 IMC, 2021 IMC, 2018 IPC; (2) all existing and new pipe to be copper above ceiling; (3) manual ball valve at technical compartment under each display case. Legend: new 2" copper pipe, manual ball valve, 2x2x2" copper tee, point of connection new to existing, 12x12 wall access panel, existing display case symbol. Right side shows a detail inset: 'DISPLAY CASE DETAIL' depicting flexible tube connection from copper pipe to display case technical compartment. Large exhibit room (auditorium/theater) is visible in the plan.

sheets.title: DISPLAY CASE LOCATION PLAN (DRAFT)
sheets.reading_notes: Preliminary/Draft document by Sandra Vicchio & Associates LLC (conservation consultant), dated 13 September 2024; survey date 11/12/24. Shows first floor plan of the Donald W. Reynolds Museum and Education Center with display case locations marked as orange squares. Blue lines indicate the existing active climate infrastructure routing. Red annotation indicates '3" copper pipe from lower level conservation machine terminates here' at upper left. Photo inset shows the lower-level conservation machine (appears to be a refrigeration/humidity control unit with white cabinet housing, copper piping, and control panel). Labels identify display case IDs (0GH-C1A, 0GH-C1, 0GH-C2, 0GH-C3, 0GH-C4, 0GH-C8, 1EL-C1, 1EL-C2, 2LV-C2, 2LV-C3, 4RL-C1, 4RL-C2, 4RL-C3, 5MV-C1, 5MV-C2, 6CL-C1, 7PR-C1, 7PR-C2, 8FA-C1). Scale 1/16" = 1'-0". This document was produced prior to BFA's engagement and served as the basis for BFA's design.

sheets.title: MECHANICAL FIRST FLOOR NEW WORK
sheets.source_file: Pages from 241011_GWMV Education Center Renovation IFC Set.pdf
sheets.reading_notes: Reference sheet from a separate project: George Washington's Mt Vernon Education Center Renovation, IFC Set dated 10/11/24. Produced by Cole&Denny Architects (333 N. Fairfax St., Alexandria VA 22314) with Ingenium Group (Washington DC) as MEP engineer, Project No. 21901.04. Shows existing HVAC equipment serving the same building: VAV boxes VAV-1 through VAV-13+, SG (supply grille) units, SS-1 split system (indoor and outdoor units), refrigerant piping between indoor evaporator and outdoor condensing unit. Key notes: reconfigure existing sprinkler per NFPA 13; provide means of dust protection; re-route condensate drain. This drawing provides context on the building's primary HVAC system (VAV-based air distribution) which is separate from the conservation climate control system BFA is working on. Not a BFA document.
